text: “NEW” BOYCOTT.

label: paragraph_title
text: Transport Union's Word Obeyed.

label: text
text: DEADLOCK IN CANTON.

label: text
text: Chinese Ships Not Taking Up

label: text
text: "Canton's "new" boycott has actually started, the order of the Transport Union being obeyed as from yesterday.

label: text
text: The result is that another deadlock—as far as merchandise is concerned—has set in at Canton, but passenger communication is still permitted.

label: text
text: Several forces of agitators are at work, each with different objects.

label: text
text: The Transport Union comprises cargo coolies and the employees of cargo junks. A resolution was passed a week ago, by over 1,000 delegates, when the handling of cargo to or from British (or Hong Kong) vessels was forbidden as from Nov. 8 (yesterday).

label: text
text: Hitherto the Steamboat Co.'s ships have carried little or no cargo down, except the usual quota of foodstuffs, shipped without recourse to members of the Transport Union, the respective shop fokis working the merchandise themselves.

label: text
text: No Shipments To-day.

label: text
text: However, the "outside" companies (i.e., the boats operated by Chinese owners, under the British flag) have done a good deal of business.

label: text
text: Yesterday evening, a report came from an authentic source that the S.S. "Tung On" (of the Tung On S.S. Co.) had been boy-cotted by the Transport Union, on arrival at Canton in the afternoon. Accordingly, the S.S. "Sai On" took up no cargo this morning.

label: text
text: As stated yesterday, the licences of the cargo junkes at Canton are issued by the Harbour authorities of the Chinese Maritime Customs and these licences contain a clause whereby they may be cancelled if the holders refused to work cargo.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hope From Government.

label: text
text: "Native merchants in Canton are also looking to the Nationalist Government to devise a speedy "settlement" by ordering the men back to work.

label: text
text: The position at present is that passengers can travel without restriction between Canton and Hong Kong either by rail or by steamer. Those who prefer the Steamboat Co.'s vessels are still subject to molestation and veiled threats, in spite of armed police patrols sent out by the Canton Government.

label: text
text: On the other hand, cargo can be sent up to other West River ports where the trouble is not so much agitation as the examination by the Government inspection corps.

label: text
text:
Two Chinese flags.
Another body of agitators—other than those picketing the Steamboat Co.'s wharves and the Transport Union—is the body pressing for the Chinese boats under British registry to change over to the Chinese flag. Others go still further. They are not satisfied with merely “the Chinese flag.” They insist that those at present under Chinese registry shall cease to fly the “Republican” five-barred ensign and hoist the “clear sky, white sun” banner of the Nationalist Government. One river steamboat has already been told that the use of the five-barred flag will be construed as “anti-Revolutionary” policy.
There is another dispute in which the rice merchants and some lightermen are concerned but this is not attributable to anti-British or anti-foreign agitation.

label: text
text: The Strike Committee talks of appointing a select committee to investigate into the fire on Saturday, when their headquarters at East Garden were burned out.

label: text
text:
It is now practically definite that there were no casualties through the blaze but it is almost impossible to account for the prisoners, in the face of the attitude of the Strike Committee.
Native traders look on the fire as a blessing in disguise.
New headquarters will be found at Whampoo. Meanwhile, a few more of the rank and its have taken advantage of the opportunity to leave without even applying for the $10 demobilisation grant.

label: paragraph_title
text: PRINCE GEORGE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Leaves for Home on

label: text
text: AFTER 1 1/2 YEARS SERVICE.

label: text
text: Sailing by "Empress of

label: text
text: H.R.H. Prince Georgia will be leaving Hong Kong and the China station for Home in the early hours of Thursday morning. He leaves by the R.M.S. "Empress of Russia" which is scheduled to leave at 1 a.m.

label: text
text: For just over one and a half years, Prince George has been attached to the China station, arriving in Hong Kong by the s.s. "Malwa" on May 28, 1925. He was entertained as a "distinguished visitor" by reason of the fact that H.M.S. "Hawkins," which he was to join, was in Shanghai.

label: text
text: On joining the flagship of the China Squadron, Prince George resumed the rank of "sub" and some months later qualified as a full Lieutenant. Except for a few occasions in which he has been ap-

label: text
text: pointed by H.M. King George to act as His Majesty's deputy in conferring honours, Prince George's position whilst ashore at Hong Kong and other South China ports has been that of Lieutenant.

label: text
text: Prince George has been exceedingly popular during his service on the China station, both among naval officers and men with whom he has come into contact and in local social circles. His readiness to participate in entertainments and dances organised by the ship's company, on board and ashore, has been much appreciated here. Prince George, during the presence of H.M.S. "Hawkins" in port, has been a familiar figure at Repulse Bay and at carnivals and dances elsewhere.

label: text
text:
During his service here, Prince George paid an official visit to Japan, and when H.M.S. "Hawkins" was in Singapore he spent some considerable time in Malaya. In addition to his service on the flagship, he also served for a period on the Yangtse gunboat "Hollyhock."
The few occasions in which Prince George has appeared in his official capacity whilst in China have been marked by a cordial and whole-hearted expression of British loyalty to the reigning house. As the Prince, at the end of his tour of duty, probably carries away the happiest of recollections, so too do the British peoples of the Far East retain pleasant memories of his visit here and with him go their best wishes for a pleasant voyage and n distinguished future.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: MURDER AND SUICIDE."

label: text
text: An inquest which held at Wandsworth to the circumstances surrounding the deaths of Mr. Roscoe Brunner, ex-Chairman of Brunner, Mond & Co., and his wife, who were found shot dead in their house at Rochampton.

label: text
text: The evidence showed that Roscoe Brunner had been in ill-health for two years. He was very depressed over serious business troubles for which he as chairman of Brunner Mond's was held responsible and had to vacate the chairmanship.

label: text
text: He was also very disappointed he was not made a director in the new amalgamation. His financial position was very sound. His wife on the day of the tragedy visited three newspaper offices.

label: text
text: Sir John Brunner testified that his wife did not accept the vacation of the chairmanship which Roscoe accepted loyally. Sir John expressed the opinion that Roscoe Brunner had learned she was visiting newspaper offices on his account, that would have been enough to turn his brain.

label: text
text:
A verdict of murder and suicide was returned.—Reuter.
[Mr. Roscoe Brunner, D.L., J.P. the second son of the Rt. Hon. Sir J. T. Brunner, the first Baronet, was born in 1871, and became a barrister, being called in 1895. His wife, whom he married in 1898, was Miss Ethel Houston, eldest daughter of the late Mr. Arthur Houston, K.C., and an authoress (author of "Celia and her Friends," etc.). They had two sons and a daughter.]

Northern Counter-Attacks on Kiuklang?
Confirmation has been received of news that Kiuklang has been captured by Southern Chinese forces.
Fighting in the neighbourhood is continuing and counter-attacks appear to be taking place.
British, French, American and Japanese Naval parties have been landed to protect foreign concerns which are reported to have suffered no damage or casualties although there has been severe firing and them.
Kiuklang is an old Treaty Fort on the south bank of the Yangtze River, used by Marathas from China to the west of China.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL HOPES.

label: text
text: SEEKING A COMPROMISE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Outline of Government's

label: text
text: The Miners' Executive considered for three hours this morning the compromise plan drafted by the Government for the settlement of the mining dispute. This afternoon they proceeded to Downing Street and submitted their views to the Premier and the Coal Committee of the Cabinet.

label: text
text: The coalowners were then summoned, and were interviewed separately. Conversations were still proceeding at half past seven this evening. From statements made by members of the Miners' Executive it would appear that important points are still in dispute.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Five Points:

label: text
text:
The Government's suggestions to end the coal dispute are believed to be on the following lines:—
(1) The minimum percentage in addition to the basis rates to be that provided in the 1921 agreement—the minimum to be paid whatever the hours worked.
(2) The ratio for the division of the proceeds of the industry between wages profits to vary between 87-13 and 86-15 according to the circumstances of each district.

label: text
text:
(3) The present mode of ascertaining the proceeds to continue.
(4) The subsistence allowance of the low paid day wage men to be retained.

label: text
text: (5) In the absence of a national agreement, a guarantee to be given to the Prime Minister from each district.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
ceeding hopefully.
The miners throughout were adamant against conceding longer hours, but a statement was issued at midnight at the conclusion of the conference between the Cabinet Ministers and the miners declaring the conference adjourned as the Miners' Executive had found it necessary to consult their constituents.

label: text
text: A miners' delegate conference is being summoned for November 10.

label: paragraph_title
text: EARLIER CABLES.

label: text
text: The Miners' Executive met this morning to consider proposals for the settlement of the coal dispute on a basis of district agreements. These proposals were drafted by the Government after conversations with both parties on Saturday. They are set out in a series of national principles to be embodied in district agreements.

label: text
text:
In submitting their conditional offer to accept the district agreements, the miners laid down demands for firstly, a national minimum percentage, secondly, a district subsistence wage, thirdly a common method of ascertainment of proceeds with a common ratio of division between wages and profits, and fourthly, a form of national co-operating machinery. The Government put these suggestions before the coal owners in a more definite form designed to replace the national co-operating body, by safeguarding more closely the observance of national principles by the district without recourse to arbitration or a national body set up by legislation.
The owners, it is stated, have fallen in with the Government's proposals to the extent of agreeing to ask their district associations to revise their terms, and reframe them on a common plan in any district agreements that may be negotiated. The Government's present idea appears to be that when it is obtained from the owners the promise will, if passed on to the miners with the full responsibility of the Government behind it, constitutes a sufficient guarantees for the miners that they will be treated fairly.
The success of the new plan to achieve a settlement depends mainly on the attitude adopted by the miners. Executive at the morning's meeting. The result will be commented to the Government this afternoon. British Wireless Services
